title: Authentication at the view boundary
summary: Require an authenticated member in one decorator and test the 401 and 200 paths with Django's test client.

scenario.briefing: The inventory JSON view is open, and request.user is read without checking whether anyone is signed in. Add one authentication boundary and prove both the anonymous and member paths.

objectives.description: Protect a view with a reusable authentication check.
Test the anonymous and authenticated paths.

hints: AuthenticationMiddleware fills request.user from the session.
Wrap the view so the check runs before the query.
Return a JSON 401 for an anonymous caller instead of redirecting an API request.
Use @wraps so the wrapped view keeps its name and metadata.

misconceptions.feedback: Every caller reaches the view until a check stops them. Apply the decorator and test the anonymous path.

misconceptions.description: Defining a guard but never applying it.
misconceptions.feedback: A decorator only runs when it wraps the view. Put @require_member above item_list.

misconceptions.description: Using login_required on a JSON API and accepting a redirect.
misconceptions.feedback: login_required redirects a browser to a login page. A JSON client needs an explicit 401 response.
The test should fail before the guard is added. Assert 401 for the anonymous caller.

misconceptions.description: Using 401 for an authenticated caller who lacks permission.
misconceptions.feedback: The caller is authenticated, so the correct response is 403. 401 is for a missing identity.

sections.title: The middleware supplies a user
sections.body: AuthenticationMiddleware reads the session cookie and assigns request.user. For an anonymous visitor it sets an AnonymousUser whose is_authenticated property is false. Middleware identifies the caller; it does not decide which views require a signed-in user.

sections.title: A decorator is a view boundary
sections.body: A decorator wraps the view function, so it can reject the request before the query runs. Returning JsonResponse with status 401 gives an API client a machine-readable answer. functools.wraps preserves the wrapped view's name and documentation.

sections.title: Authentication and permission are separate
sections.body: is_authenticated answers whether the caller signed in. A permission answers whether that identity may perform the action. An authenticated user without inventory.view_item gets 403 when permission_required is configured with raise_exception=True; a missing identity gets 401.

vocabulary.definition: Django middleware that attaches the session user to each request.
A function that wraps another function to add behavior around it.
The status for a request that has not authenticated.
The status for a known identity that lacks permission.

hints: The test client can sign a user in with force_login.

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse


class InventoryAuthTests(TestCase):
    def test_anonymous_request_is_rejected(self):
        # TODO: assert that the API rejects anonymous callers
        response = self.client.get(reverse("item-list"))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)

steps.title: Transfer to a missing permission
steps.prompt: A signed-in staff user lacks the inventory.view_item permission. The view uses @permission_required("inventory.view_item", raise_exception=True). Which response is correct?
hints: The missing piece is a permission, not an identity.
raise_exception=True turns PermissionDenied into a response.

quiz.prompt: A signed-in staff user lacks the inventory.view_item permission. The view uses @permission_required("inventory.view_item", raise_exception=True). Which response is correct?

options.label: 403 because the user is authenticated but lacks the permission.
302 to the login page because the permission is missing.
200 because staff users bypass view permissions.

quiz.explanation: Authentication succeeded, so the identity is known. A missing permission produces PermissionDenied, and raise_exception=True turns it into 403. Staff status does not grant every model permission.
